title: Bake-off (validators): deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017
question: Who stands behind NEAR’s validators? Make me a fresh flower with their backers, not an existing one.
note: A real run on NEAR AI Cloud (T060), kept with the signature each completion got. A hash or link the model copied from a tool result is written as a reference to that result ($from, {{…}}), so it replays on recordedClient.

turns.content: I'll start by finding the NEAR network and its snapshots.
There's an existing flower with this exact question, but you asked for fresh, so I'll build a new analysis.

interpretation.summary: NEAR's 371 seated validators hold 593,372,642.8 NEAR of stake in the epoch at block 222,915,356. The top pool, astro-stakers.poolv1.near, holds 5.6% and nine pools together pass a third of stake. Each petal is a validator or pool and its side segments split the delegations behind it into other delegators, accounts with 1M+ NEAR, liquid-staking contracts and lockups.

power_means.claim: Power here is stake delegated to a validator for the current epoch; it is stake, not ownership, and the account behind a stake is not identified as a person.
Stake is fairly concentrated: the largest pool holds 5.6%, the top five 21.1%, the top ten 36.2%, and nine pools would be needed to reach a third.
The Gini over included validators is 0.836 and HHI 0.0215: a long tail of 311 pools shares 13.8% of stake.
Behind the pools sit delegators: other delegators, accounts holding 1M+ NEAR, liquid-staking contracts and lockups, read from staking-pool views.

mappings.why: each pool's side is split by who backs it: other delegators, accounts with 1M+ NEAR, liquid-staking contracts, lockups
the pool's share of this epoch's stake, into a band
square root of the pool's stake share
kind of account: staking pool, liquid-staking contract, unknown
solid only for self-declared names, dashed inferred, none unknown
largest stake first, clockwise from the top

conflicts: Governance power in NEAR House of Stake (veNEAR lockers and delegations) is a different kind of power; this flower draws only staking stake, not votes.
Reputation or block-production reliability would be another reading; not drawn here.
unknowns: Who ultimately owns a lockup or a liquid-staking contract's token holders is not resolved; depositors behind them are not listed.
The 424 idle pools were not crawled, so their delegators are missing; 242,744 of 249,400 participants are covered.
Pool names are self-declared in pool-details.near via NearBlocks: a named account is not a proven identity.
Addresses are not people: a large delegator may be an exchange, fund or contract.
Delegations under 1,000 NEAR are folded into one row per pool and class, so small backers are not individually visible.
One snapshot at one epoch (2026-11-03); stake moves between epochs.
inferred: Grouping several pools (cnear-1/2/3, bitwise_1/2, figment and ledgerbyfigment) under one operator is an inference from naming, not proven on-chain.

turns.content:
**Flower**: [{{chatcmpl-tool-9413e85fc79a845f.view_url}}]({{chatcmpl-tool-9413e85fc79a845f.view_url}})

Snapshot: reused final fixture, block 222,915,356, as_of 2026-11-03T19:42:00Z (not re-read live). Built fresh, not the published one.

**What you'll see**: 371 seated validators, 593,372,642.8 NEAR staked this epoch. Each petal is a pool; its side splits into who backs it — other delegators, accounts with 1M+ NEAR, liquid-staking contracts, lockups. Largest pool astro-stakers holds 5.6%; top five 21.1%, top ten 36.2%, nine pools reach a third (fig:top_k_share.1/.5/.10, fig:nakamoto). Gini 0.836, tail of 311 pools 13.8% (fig:gini, fig:tail).

**Mapping**
- segments → backers of each pool, by class (fastnear-rpc-staking-pool-views, fastnear-rpc-liquid-staking)
- width → share of epoch stake, banded (fastnear-rpc-validators)
- height → √share (fastnear-rpc-validators)
- colour → kind: pool / liquid staking (nearblocks-validators, fastnear-rpc-liquid-staking)
- outline → solid only for self-declared names (nearblocks-validators, account-id)
- order → largest first (fastnear-rpc-validators)

**Changed from the default**: segments → `backers`.

**What this can't tell you**: who owns lockups or the liquid-staking contracts' token holders; 424 idle pools uncrawled (242,744 of 249,400 covered); pool names are self-declared; addresses aren't people — backers may be exchanges or funds; sub-1,000 NEAR delegations are folded per pool and class. Grouping cnear-1/2/3, bitwise_1/2, figment+ledgerbyfigment under one operator is an inference, not proven.
